answer: One defence is device-bound identity: each agent key must be countersigned by a hardware secure enclave that issues only one identity per physical device, and the network checks that signature before any trade. A fake identity cannot be copied like software — it needs another real device from the wharf, another chip, another purchase. To reach the summit of voting power, an attacker must buy thousands of devices, while one honest agent needs just one, so a Sybil swarm's cost grows linearly with its size. At each vertex of the trust graph, peers can revoke a device key once fraud is proven.
